title: Sharp Self-Chollet Inequalities in Order Five: Rank Two and Structured Rank Three
content: For a real correlation matrix $C$, the self-conjugate specialization of Chollet's conjecture asserts \permanent(C\circ C)\leq\permanent(C)^2$. We determine the sharp constant in order five under the rank-two constraint: \\\\$\permanent(C\circ C)\leq \dfrac{137}{1440}\,\permanent(C)^2$, \\$C\in\R^{5\times5},\qquad C\succeq0,\qquad\diagC=\mathbf1,\qquad \rank C\leq2$.\\ Equality holds exactly when the five Gram lines form a regular pentagon in $\mathbb{RP}^1$, up to permutation and sign switching. The proof reduces the two permanents to elementary symmetric functions of five unimodular numbers, solves the remaining two-phase minimization, and ends with explicit sum-of-squares and positive-semidefinite Gram certificates. We then study the rank-three stratum. The matrix\\ $J_2\oplus\left(\begin{array}{ccc} 1&-1/2&-1/2\\ -1/2&1&-1/2\\ -1/2&-1/2&1 \end{array}\right)$\ has self-Chollet ratio $13/48$. We prove that this value is sharp in two infinite structured rank-three families and that the displayed configuration is a strict local maximum in the full rank-three configuration space. We also prove Chollet's inequality whenever $|c_{ij}|\leq27/50$ for $i\ne j$, with the sharper estimate $\mathcal R(C)\leq621/800$ at coherence $1/2$. Finally, without a rank assumption, Chollet's inequality is strict away from the identity whenever $\lambda_{\min}(C)\geq3/4$. The proposed global rank-three value $13/48$ remains open. All finite algebraic certificates are supplied in exact arithmetic.
